approachQuestion.prompt:
Three-way parity. Each entry is A, B or C. Count nonempty contiguous intervals in which all three symbols appear equally often. Return a count.

Input: labels=[A,B,C,A,B,C]. Output: 5.

Constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000. Labels are exactly A,B,C; counts and answer fit 64 bits. Hash operations on fixed-size integer pairs take expected constant time including amortized resizing.

Which approach handles the complete task correctly and efficiently?

options.text: Maintain cumulative counts a,b,c and a frequency map keyed by (a-b,a-c), seeded with (0,0):1. After each symbol, add the prior frequency of the new pair to the answer, then increment it.
options.feedback: Equal difference pairs at two boundaries mean the three count increments are equal. Querying before insertion excludes empty intervals.

options.text: Key the map only by a-b and count repeated keys.
options.feedback: For [A,B], a-b returns to zero, but no C appears: the interval is not balanced among all three symbols.

options.text: Enumerate every interval, counting its three symbols and testing equality.
options.feedback: This gives correct results, but repeatedly traverses overlapping candidates. The selected summary reuses their shared work.

details: Maintain cumulative counts a,b,c and a frequency map keyed by (a-b,a-c), seeded with (0,0):1. After each symbol, add the prior frequency of the new pair to the answer, then increment it.

Equal differences (a-b,a-c) at two boundaries imply all three counts increased equally between them. A single difference would allow the third category to vary unchecked. Frequencies count every matching earlier boundary.

feedback.reason: Hash fixed-size difference pairs rather than storing candidate intervals.
details: Each fixed-size pair lookup/update takes expected constant time, giving expected O(n) total. At most n+1 keys are stored.

Use expected constant-time hashing of two-word keys including amortized resizing; worst-case constant time is not guaranteed. Arithmetic is constant time; exclude input and scalar output, include map storage and no recursive stack.

Each of n symbols updates a fixed-size two-word difference key and performs a bounded number of expected-amortized constant-time map operations. Time is expected O(n), not a worst-case O(n) guarantee for every hash behavior. Counts aggregate many matching boundaries at once; no quadratic enumeration of interval endpoints occurs.

Up to n+1 distinct difference-pair keys and their frequencies remain in the map, giving O(n) auxiliary space. The expected-linear/O(1)-space option drops this growing state. The quadratic-time/constant-space option neither matches the shared map scan nor accounts for its storage. Input symbols and the scalar count are excluded; map entries are included.
